title: EATF Action Evidence Package toolkit
description: Open toolkit for creating, inspecting, and offline-verifying Action Evidence Packages (.aep): a hybrid RSA-4096 plus ML-DSA-65 signer, two verifiers (TypeScript and Python), both built by Tyche Institute, sign/verify/inspect CLIs, RFC 9881 public-key encoding, JSON schemas, positive and negative conformance vectors, and a deterministic offline downgrade lab.
notes: Version 0.7.1 makes both verifiers (TypeScript and Python, both built by Tyche Institute) reject malformed ML-DSA-65 entries with valid=false and a shared first-failure code, with or without --pqc-signer-key. In v0.7.0 and earlier a signature_pqc.sig that is not base64 crashed both verifiers, an unusable pqc_public_key.pem crashed the Python verifier, and some malformed signatures and empty entries were accepted by one verifier and rejected by the other. New failure code PQC_SIGNATURE_ENCODING; one byte-level decoding rule for signature_pqc.sig in both languages; an empty ML-DSA entry now counts as present in Python, as it already did in TypeScript; a Python cryptography backend without ML-DSA support reports PQC_SUPPORT_UNAVAILABLE. The 5 accepted and 8 rejected conformance vectors, the 42 lab observations and the 21 decision-path cases give the same results as in v0.7.0. Previous version v0.7.0 is doi:10.5281/zenodo.23451134 under concept doi:10.5281/zenodo.21763055; releases through v0.5.0 remain under earlier concept doi:10.5281/zenodo.21511608.
